hypothesis: reinvesting sparse-backward savings in a larger batch can reduce gradient variance instead of merely buying more optimizer steps

execution.sparse_arms: dense forward with gathered 50% FFN backward and inverse-activity scale 2
execution.dense_arms: ordinary dense forward and backward at both batch sizes
execution.ema: identical final 0.95 EMA for every arm with no decay sweep or checkpoint selection
execution.deployment: ordinary dense inference with averaged weights

cost_accounting.training: realized-row CPU-calibrated formulas scaled to each arm's actual batch size
cost_accounting.auxiliary_operations: actual scoring, gather/scatter and gradient scaling for sparse arms; two EMA operations per parameter per step for every arm
cost_accounting.data_accounting: training sequence counts reported per arm; generated data are not held out as a compute-free resource
cost_accounting.evaluation: identical final held-out batches, reported separately from training-plus-EMA cost

primary_endpoint: final EMA ordinary dense held-out loss at training-plus-scaling-plus-EMA cost

decision_rules.allocation_failure: low_max_abs does not beat random at the same batch size despite random receiving more steps and sequences; stop
decision_rules.no_level_3: low_max_abs fails to beat either dense batch-32 or dense batch-40 EMA; stop
decision_rules.development_level_3: low_max_abs loss is below random and both dense arms while total cost is no greater than every control
decision_rules.confirmation: only development_level_3 launches the identical four-arm body-7 comparison

prohibited: changing batch size, activity, scale, steps, EMA decay, or evaluation after launch
launching body 7 without a development-level win over every control
